context_purpose: The committee wants each eligible household to cast one valid vote on a levy or rule change.

norm_violation_today.reason: Condominium votes are run by the committee itself, which is entitled to know who is eligible and usually to record who voted, so collecting name and unit is in-norm; only the ID-card photo is over-collection.

purpose_sufficiency.lost: A telco uniqueness proof does not show residency or ownership weighting and may not satisfy signed or recorded vote rules, so eligibility and auditability are lost.

transmission_check.reason: Condominium rules may require recorded or signed votes with ownership weights, and I cannot confirm whether an anonymous ballot would be accepted.

context_purpose: The telecom wants to confirm the applicant is a genuine enrolled student before granting a discounted plan, and avoid identity fraud.

norm_violation_today.reason: The operator is entitled to real-name ID data for SIM registration, but student number and uploaded student-card photos go beyond what is needed for the discount.

purpose_sufficiency.lost: Little is lost for the discount step; the operator still needs its separate real-name registration, which the proof does not replace.

transmission_check.reason: SIM registration is understood to require collecting ID data regardless, though the student-discount step itself is a voluntary commercial offer.

context_purpose: The community committee wants one ballot per eligible resident without publicly tying votes to individuals.

norm_violation_today.reason: The committee is the legitimate organiser and is entitled to name, unit and contact details for eligibility; exposing them to the administrator is within the context's norms.

purpose_sufficiency.lost: A telco uniqueness proof cannot show residence or ownership-weighted voting rights, which the committee needs for valid outcomes.

transmission_check.reason: Condominium rules on weighted and recorded voting may require identity-linked records, and I cannot confirm what is required.

context_purpose: The private operator wants assurance of payment reliability before extending a childcare or bus service contract.

norm_violation_today.reason: Requesting bank statements and employment proof to screen parents for solvency goes beyond what childcare enrolment norms support.

purpose_sufficiency.lost: Absence from the debtor register says nothing about future payment capacity, which is what the operator actually wants.

transmission_check.reason: No legal duty appears to require the operator to collect this, so any lighter flow is permitted, though the screening itself may be unlawful or discriminatory.

context_purpose: The operator must make sure that people working with children are not barred from such work by child-protection or sexual-offence registers.

norm_violation_today.reason: A good-conduct certificate reveals the full criminal-record status, including old or unrelated entries, when only the restriction-list status is relevant.

purpose_sufficiency.lost: A stale holder-presented proof misses entries added after signing, and an authority-run query may be required instead.

transmission_check.reason: Child-protection rules appear to oblige employers to run specific checks through official channels, and I cannot confirm whether a holder-presented proof would be accepted.

context_purpose: The host library or facility wants to give access only to genuine members of a partner university and manage its resources.

norm_violation_today.reason: Registering a visitor with national ID or passport and keeping a lending record tied to it is plausible for a library, but linking reading history to a national ID goes beyond what is needed.

purpose_sufficiency.lost: The host loses a stable identity for chasing overdue or lost items unless it keeps its own visitor account.

transmission_check.reason: Reciprocal access is a voluntary service arrangement, and I know of no legal duty to collect national ID for it.

context_purpose: The landlord wants to know that the tenant is still employed and can keep paying rent, as a condition of the reduced deposit.

norm_violation_today.reason: Collecting salary band, ID number and enrolment details, often kept in chat logs, exceeds what a continuing-employment check requires.

purpose_sufficiency.lost: Employment status does not show income level or ability to pay, and the landlord still needs the tenant's name for the lease.

transmission_check.reason: The landlord's request is a voluntary condition for a deposit benefit, with no statute I know of requiring the full certificate.

context_purpose: The bureau wants to confirm that applicants are currently enrolled and are registered local residents so the programme reaches its intended group.

norm_violation_today.reason: A full household transcript exposes parents and siblings who are irrelevant to an enrolment-plus-residency test.

purpose_sufficiency.lost: Many programmes also need income or family data for eligibility, which this proof does not carry.

transmission_check.reason: Agencies may be entitled to pull household data directly with consent, and I cannot confirm whether programme rules require the full transcript.
